==English== ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:quiete>>>|:root|ine-pro:*kʷyeh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|quiete}}, from {{der|en|fro|quiet|pos=adjective}} and {{m|fro|quiete|pos=noun}}, from {{der|en|la|quiētus}}, past participle of {{m|la|quiesco|quiēscere|to keep quiet, rest}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kʷyeh₁-||rest}}. {{doublet|en|coy|quit|quite|quietus}}. Largely displaced native {{noncog|en|still}} in the sense of "with little or no sound". ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˈkwaɪ̯.ət/|[ˈkʰw̥aɪ̯.ət]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-quiet.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|aɪət|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|qui|et}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj|er,more}} # With little or no sound; free of [[disturb]]ing [[noise]]. #: {{syn|en|hushed|muffled|Thesaurus:quiet}} #: {{ant|en|loud|Thesaurus:noisy}} #: {{ux|en|I can't hear the music; it is too '''quiet'''.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|author=Donald Appleyard|title=Livable Streets|page=98 |passage=On the light streets, better streetcleaners, more trees, more police, and '''quieter''' buses were the most popular improvements, followed by cutting down the number of cars and improving children's play space.}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=w:William Safire|title=Essay; The Quiet Noisemaker|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1999/04/05/opinion/essay-the-quiet-noisemaker.html|date=05-04-1999|passage=Before long, the unsuspecting salesman was earnestly pitching him "the '''quietest''' noisemaker on the market."|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231231003225/https://www.nytimes.com/1999/04/05/opinion/essay-the-quiet-noisemaker.html|archivedate=31 December 2023}} # Having little [[motion]] or [[activity]]; [[calm]]. #: {{syn|en|placid|serene|Thesaurus:calm}} #: {{ux|en|the sea was '''quiet'''}} #: {{ux|en|a '''quiet''' night at home}} #: {{ux|en|all '''quiet''' on the Western front}} # Not [[busy]], of low [[quantity]]. #: {{syn|en|slow|unbusy|Thesaurus:inactive}} #: {{ux|en|The traffic was '''quiet''' for a Monday morning.}} #: {{ux|en|Business was '''quiet''' for the season.}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=8|passage=It was a casual sneer, obviously one of a long line. There was hatred behind it, but of a '''quiet''', chronic type, nothing new or unduly virulent, and he was taken aback by the flicker of amazed incredulity that passed over the younger man's ravaged
